articles.title: Mercury dips to single digits in high ranges of Keralam, ushering in early onset of winter chill - The Hindu
articles.full_text:
Heralding the onset of winter, temperatures have begun to dip in the high ranges and midlands of Keralam, bringing a noticeable chill to mornings and nights, particularly in central and northern parts of the State.
The weakening of easterly winds and the resulting atmospheric stability have created favourable conditions for the early onset of winter-like weather in the State, with temperatures expected to fall further in the coming days.
Recorded temperature
The mercury dropped to single digits at several places in Idukki on Saturday (November 14), with the premises of Kundala dam recording the lowest minimum temperature of 7.9°C, followed by Munnar at 9.7°C. Kuppady in Wayanad also recorded a minimum temperature of 13.7°C on Saturday, while the midland regions of the State have been experiencing a moderate chill. Vellanikkara in Thrissur recorded 20.8°C, followed by Punalur in Kollam at 21°C, with both places recording temperatures around 2–3°C below the seasonal average.
Weak easterly winds, coupled with clear skies over most parts of the State, except the southern districts, have favoured the early formation of fog during the mornings. However, the maritime influence in the midland and coastal regions moderated the impact of the winter-like conditions.
Cyclonic systems
Speaking to The Hindu, Neetha K. Gopal, Director of the India Meteorological department (IMD), Keralam, said that although successive cyclonic systems were forming over the Bay of Bengal, including another system expected to develop by November 16, they were unlikely to have any significant impact on the weather over Keralam with the systems taking a recurve before making landfall, leaving less impact on the State.
However, isolated rainfall triggered by easterly waves is likely at some places during the remaining period of the northeast monsoon. Any influx of moisture into the atmosphere over Keralam would temporarily reduce the morning chill. Otherwise, winter-like conditions are expected to prevail across the State over the next few weeks, Ms. Gopal said.
El Niño impact
Although winter-like conditions have set in slightly earlier than usual this year, the seasonal rainfall deficit during the northeast monsoon (October–December) raises concerns over the months ahead. The strengthening El Niño in the equatorial Pacific, which disrupts global wind and atmospheric circulation patterns, increases the likelihood of a relatively mild winter and raises the risk of extreme heat, including heatwave conditions, during the summer of 2027. This could result in above-normal minimum and maximum temperatures across much of the country, experts said.
The northeast monsoon is already 21% deficient in Keralam, with the State receiving only 321 mm of rainfall against the normal of 404.3 mm during the season so far. The deficit is likely to widen further during the remaining period of the season as easterly winds weaken over the State.
